The severity of the text artifact is catastrophic for a document class, warranting a high penalty.
alignment_reasoning: While the 'fine_grained_classifier' correctly identifies the image as a 'menu' (Top-1), this is likely due to the global layout (columns, beige background) rather than semantic content. The core functional requirement of a menu—legible text listing items—is completely failed. The text is structurally melted and semantically void (gibberish). Therefore, despite the correct class label prediction, the image fails to conform to the taxonomy's definition of a 'listing of available food and beverage items'. It is a visual hallucination of a menu, not a functional one.

The OCR expert returned nonsensical strings with low confidence, confirming the text is not just blurry but structurally invalid. These are significant structural failures for a document-based object.
